subject: Finlatech — Dedicated capacity demo & throughput fit
body:
--- Message 1 (original inbound) ---
From: Elinor Park <elinor@finlatech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in dedicated capacity for low-latency, high-throughput use case

Hi Karthik,

We spun up a few self-serve tests on Redwood and are seeing promising fidelity, but our production workload needs dedicated capacity. Goal: ~1,200 QPS sustained (peaks to ~1.8k QPS), median generation latency < 120ms for 256 token sequences.

Can we schedule a dedicated-capacity walkthrough this week so we can validate throughput runbooks, SLA/COR, and networking (VPC peering)? My R&D ops lead (ops@finlatech.com) should join. Prefer PST mornings.

Quick background: we run customer-facing recommendation API, average prompt length ~180 tokens; we also batch internal indexing requests. We care about cold-start tail and KV cache warmup.

Thanks,
Elinor Park
Head of ML Platforms
Finlatech

--- Message 2 (SDR outreach) ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elinor Park <elinor@finlatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in dedicated capacity for low-latency, high-throughput use case

Hi Elinor — great to meet you over email, and glad the self-serve tests looked useful. I’ll coordinate a dedicated walkthrough focused on throughput, latency SLOs, and the VPC setup.

Before we lock a slot can you fill the attached Throughput_Worksheet.xlsx with:
- expected sustained qps and peak qps by endpoint
- average & p95 sequence lengths
- concurrency patterns (many small requests vs few large batches)
- which model family you plan to use (or open to Redwood recommendations)

I’m Cc’ing Ben from our scheduling team to propose times. We can also share a short Dedicated_Specs.pdf with hardware/quantization options post-call.

Proposed slots (PST):
- Thu Aug 6, 10:00–10:45
- Thu Aug 6, 14:00–14:45
- Fri Aug 7, 09:00–09:45

If none of those work, tell Ben what works and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Throughput_Worksheet.xlsx

--- Message 3 (scheduling confirmation) ---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elinor Park <elinor@finlatech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in dedicated capacity for low-latency, high-throughput use case

Hi Elinor — happy to schedule. I’ve penciled in Thu Aug 6 at 10:00 PDT (30–45m).
Calendar link / invite: https://calendar.redwoodinference.com/book?slot=2026-08-06T10:00Z

Please accept the invite. If you haven’t yet, attach the throughput worksheet — it helps our infra team size the run.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
SDR, Redwood Inference

--- Message 4 (reschedule request) ---
From: Elinor Park <elinor@finlatech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in dedicated capacity for low-latency, high-throughput use case

Thanks Ben — quick update: our CTO has a mandatory all-hands at 10am PST and needs to be on the call. Could we move to Thu Aug 6, 14:00 PDT instead? Also looping our R&D Ops alias for networking questions (ops@finlatech.com).

Apologies for the short notice — would prefer the later slot if still available.

On Wed, Aug 5, 2026 at 4:02 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Elinor — great to meet you over email, and glad the self-serve tests looked useful. I’ll coordinate a dedicated walkthrough focused on throughput, latency SLOs, and the VPC setup.
> 
> Before we lock a slot can you fill the attached Throughput_Worksheet.xlsx with:
> - expected sustained qps and peak qps by endpoint
> - average & p95 sequence lengths
> - concurrency patterns (many small requests vs few large batches)
> - which model family you plan to use (or open to Redwood recommendations)
> 
> I’m Cc’ing Ben from our scheduling team to propose times. We can also share a short Dedicated_Specs.pdf with hardware/quantization options post-call.
> 
> Proposed slots (PST):
> - Thu Aug 6, 10:00–10:45
> - Thu Aug 6, 14:00–14:45
> - Fri Aug 7, 09:00–09:45
> 
> Best,
> Karthik

--- Message 5 (final confirmation & prep) ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elinor Park <elinor@finlatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, R&D Ops <ops@finlatech.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in dedicated capacity for low-latency, high-throughput use case

Thanks — Thu Aug 6, 14:00 PDT works. I’ve updated the invite to that slot and added Vanessa (our Dedicated PM) and our infra lead.

Prep & ask list for the call:
- Please upload the filled Throughput_Worksheet.xlsx to the invite or reply here.
- If you have a short traffic sample (ndjson or CSV) that shows qps/time, please share — helps us size warm caches.
- Let us know which model family (Llama2/OPT/Redwood-verified) you prefer; if undecided we’ll recommend quantization + kernel profile.

Attached is the Dedicated_Specs.pdf with an overview of GPU types, autoscale behavior, and expected per-token latency profiles for common model sizes.

Call details: Thu Aug 6, 14:00–14:45 PDT — Zoom link in calendar invite.

Looking forward — we’ll aim to have a sizing recommendation by EOD next day if you can share the worksheet.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0194
Attachments: Dedicated_Specs.pdf
